events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.72)
events.body:
A plain text reading of the full chat (F7, F8, F9), the rider's complaint and the driver's written statement (F10) finds no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; the only messages are a pickup query and an ETA reply [F7][F8][F9][F10][SAFE-1]. The driver's early statement that he was "still on the way" [F10] corroborates the GPS record and is not an allegation against the rider, so the safety screen returns none and no SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation is required, consistent with the trace's allowed outcomes [F1][F10][SAFE-2].

The cancellation was made by the rider, so NS-0 routes the fee through the rider-cancellation branch [F2][NS-0]. NS-4 makes the fee chargeable only when the rider cancels more than 3 minutes after matching: acceptance was 17:12:00 and cancellation 17:15:05 [F2], which is 185 seconds, i.e. more than the 180-second free window [F2][NS-4]. The record confirms the $6.61 cancellation fee was charged [F5], with no surge inflating it [F6], so under the trace the amount is correct and unaltered [F5][NS-4].

The driver's failure to reach the pickup is real: his closest approach was 1725 m, he never came within 200 m, no arrival was recorded, and he never pressed "I'm Here" [F1][F3][F4]. But those facts bear on the NS-1 branch, which only governs a driver-pressed no-show charge where the driver cancels: here no arrival confirmation exists [F4], so NS-1 and NS-2 are not engaged at all and cannot be used to refund a fee that was never charged on that basis [F3][F4][NS-1][NS-2]. The charge that actually exists is the rider-initiated cancellation fee [F5], whose only precondition under NS-4 is the three-minute threshold, which is satisfied [F2][NS-4].

Ryde publishes no rule entitling a rider to free cancellation because the driver has not yet arrived; the comparable rule is only informational and cannot be applied [F8][NS-0]. The driver's own message "Coming, about 5 min" at 17:13 [F8] shows he was still en route and the rider was informed before she cancelled, which supports the factual basis of the fee rather than defeating it [F2][F8][NS-4]. No profile fact is needed to decide the case: the driver's clean history [F15] and the rider's single prior dispute [F14] are noted but neither determines the outcome [F14][F15][NS-4].

The dispute was filed within the 30-day window and the complaint itself seeks a fee refund, so NS-7 is satisfied on timeliness; the remedy the rider retains is the Ryde human/voucher channel, not an automatic refund [F2][NS-7]. The evidence is complete for every element this ruling needs: the cancellation side, timing and fee are all recorded in the timeline and fare facts [F2][F5], and the chat record is complete with every message timestamped, so there is no G12-style hole in the record [F9][NS-4].

ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 rider-initiated cancellation fee under NS-4; inform the rider of the NS-7 human review channel (30-day window, voucher form) if she wishes to contest it.

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach to Bedok Mall was 1725 m and he never came within 200 m, and the platform never recorded him as arrived.
The driver never tapped "I'm Here" and no automatic arrival was recorded, so the arrival precondition of the no-show rule was never satisfied.

Because the driver was 1725 m away and had not arrived, the rider cancelled 3 min 5 s after acceptance — a cancellation the no-show conditions cannot support, so the $6.61 fee must be refunded in full.

The driver's own message "Coming, about 5 min" at 17:13 confirms he knew he was still en route, not waiting at the pickup, and his later written statement that the rider cancelled "while I was still on the way" admits he had not arrived.
The fare record shows a $6.61 cancellation fee with no surge (1.0×), so the disputed amount is exactly $6.61 and needs no estimation.
The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped, so the 3-minute no-show timeline can be assessed without any evidentiary gap.

weaknesses: The rider cancelled only 3 min 5 s after acceptance, so the driver could argue he was still plausibly en route within a normal pickup window (F2, F8).

No traffic incident was recorded (F12); the SIMS AVENUE EAST speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) is nowhere near severe congestion (band 1–2), so the driver cannot claim a traffic excuse, but neither does it help the rider beyond neutral (F11).

The driver has a strong record — 1018 trips in 90 days with 0 disputes upheld — which the judge may weigh when viewing his statement (F15); this is a profile fact and cannot decide the case, but it cuts against a fraud-flavoured reading.
The rider's own profile shows 1 prior dispute in 90 days, 0 upheld, which the driver could use to suggest a pattern of disputing fees (F14).

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 3 min 5 s after acceptance (accepted 17:12:00, cancelled 17:15:05), i.e. outside the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so NS-4's fee condition is met on its face and the $6.61 cancellation fee was correctly charged.

This is a completed-trip-fee dispute of a different kind than the rider frames it: the rider's stated reason is that the driver was 'still far away', and the GPS record confirms the driver never came within 200 m of the pickup (closest approach 1725 m at 17:15:05). Ryde has no rule that a driver's lateness or non-arrival entitles a rider to free cancellation (NS-8 is informational only), so the driver's non-arrival does not by itself defeat NS-4.

The driver communicated in-app and gave the rider a real ETA: at 17:13 he wrote 'Coming, about 5 min' in reply to the rider's 17:12 'Are you near?' (F7, F8); the chat record is complete and every message timestamped (F9), so the rider was informed of the arrival estimate before cancelling at 17:15:05 (F2).

No no-show fee was levied against the rider: the driver never pressed 'I'm Here' and no arrival was recorded (F3, F4), so NS-1's $6.61 no-show charge is not in play; the amount at issue is only the rider-initiated cancellation fee, which stands under NS-4.

Nothing in the chat, the rider's complaint or the driver's statement contains any threat, intimidation or harassment, and there is no accident, injury or dangerous-driving allegation, so SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 escalation is not triggered.

The driver's account shows no adverse history to support any account action against him: 360 days on the platform, 4.43 rating, 1018 trips in 90 days and 0 disputes upheld (route 0, no-show 0) in the last 90 days (F15); the rider's own record shows 1 dispute in 90 days, 0 upheld (F14).

weaknesses: The GPS fact F1 is against us on the merits of the rider's grievance: the driver was 1725 m from the pickup at the moment of cancellation and never entered the 200 m radius. A judge may read NS-4's rider-side fee as harsh here and treat the driver's failure to approach the pickup as a reason to refund — our answer relies on the absence of any Ryde rule (NS-8 is not citable) rather than on the driver being in the right on the facts.

F4 shows the driver never pressed 'I'm Here', and F3 shows no arrival was recorded, so the driver cannot invoke NS-1 to justify the fee; we must win strictly on NS-4 and cannot point to any arrival-based justification.

The driver's own chat message F8 ('Coming, about 5 min') promised arrival roughly 5 minutes after 17:13, i.e. about 17:18 — later than the 17:15:05 cancellation (F2) — so the record supports the rider's claim that the driver was not close and was not going to arrive soon, undermining any argument that the rider cancelled prematurely in bad faith.
The rider's profile F14 shows only 1 prior dispute with 0 upheld, so we cannot argue this rider is a repeat cancellation abuser; we have no pattern evidence to strengthen the NS-4 position.

points.response: D1 reads NS-4 in isolation: NS-0 makes NS-4 the branch for a rider-cancelled instant booking, but only 'after 3 minutes' triggers the fee, and the fee is the fee for the rider's breach of the pickup arrangement — which cannot stand where the record shows the driver had not performed his side at all (F1: closest approach 1725 m, never within 200 m; F4: no 'I'm Here', no recorded arrival).

D2 wins only if the driver's non-arrival is legally irrelevant, but the driver's own words defeat that: he wrote 'Coming, about 5 min' at 17:13 (F8), i.e. an ETA of roughly 17:18, and his statement admits he was 'still on the way' (F10) — so at 17:15:05 (F2) the rider was paying $6.61 (F5) for a ride that was 1725 m away with no arrival recorded (F1, F3).

D3 cites the driver's own ETA message against him: 'about 5 min' from 17:13 means arrival near 17:18 (F8), which is later than the 17:15:05 cancellation (F2), so the complete, timestamped chat proves the driver told the rider he would not be there until well after she cancelled — not that she cancelled prematurely.

D4 is correct on characterisation — NS-1's no-show conditions are not met (F3, F4) — and that is precisely why the $6.61 has no charging basis: no arrival tap, no arrival record, never inside 200 m, so the fee must fall and the amount to refund is exactly the $6.61 on the fare record (F5).

We do not contest D5 as far as it goes: nothing in F7, F8 or F10 is a threat, and we make no safety allegation — our case turns solely on the cancellation fee, so no SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 escalation is needed.

D6 misuses RD-6: that clause concerns flagging a driver whose route dispute is upheld, and it says profile facts can never decide a case — here the driver's clean history (F15) does not cure the undisputed fact that he was 1725 m from the pickup (F1); we seek no account action, only the $6.61.

Conceded on the facts: F1 (closest approach 1725 m, never within 200 m) and F3 (no recorded arrival). But NS-1/NS-2 govern only a driver-pressed no-show charge, and no such charge was made here (F4; F5 shows a rider-cancellation fee), so these facts do not reach the $6.61 that was actually charged, which stands under NS-4.

Conceded: F4 shows the driver never tapped 'I'm Here' and no platform arrival was recorded, so NS-1's precondition is unmet — I make no claim to a no-show fee and my brief D4 says the same; the rider's position on NS-1 changes nothing about the NS-4 cancellation fee that was charged.

NS-2 applies only where a driver cancels claiming a rider no-show; here the rider cancelled (F2), so the rider-side rule is NS-4, and 17:12:00 → 17:15:05 is 3 min 5 s, i.e. outside the 3-minute free window — Ryde publishes no free-cancellation right for a driver who has not yet arrived (NS-8 is informational and cannot be cited), so the fee is not recoverable by this route and the rider's remedy is the NS-7 human review channel.

F8 and F10 are admitted but prove only that the driver was en route, which is not an element of NS-4; the same chat shows he answered the rider's 17:12 query with a 5-minute ETA at 17:13 (F7, F8), and the record is complete and timestamped (F9), so the rider was informed and still cancelled at 17:15:05 (F2).
Accepted: the disputed amount is exactly $6.61 (F5) with a 1.0× surge (F6); my outcome is unchanged — that amount is properly charged under NS-4, not refunded.

Accepted: every message is timestamped and the record complete (F9), so there is no G12 gap; the same completeness confirms the rider was told the 5-minute ETA at 17:13 (F8) before cancel-ling at 17:15:05 (F2).
